first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because Santorini is the island everyone in the family names first. The first screen is calm and ordered: legal or symbolic, season, setting, guests. No 'affordable', no prices, no gushing, which I appreciate. Her summary for me: very good on weather and paperwork, but the caldera spaces seat 15 to 60, the biggest terrace listed takes about 100, and the article itself suggests Mykonos or Paros if the numbers are larger. I read the venue, guest list and house-rules sections myself to see if there was a way to make 300 work.

journey.quote: Take them in that order and each one narrows the next.
journey.reaction: Composed, no selling. My assistant could summarise the whole structure in one line, which is how I like to receive things.

journey.quote: Plenty of couples sign the legal paperwork in Australia, quietly, and then hold the ceremony everyone travels for in Santorini.
journey.reaction: Quietly is the right word. We would do the legal part privately at home and keep the island for the family. This reads like someone who understands that.

journey.quote: Grace Hotel in Imerovigli offers a unity ceremony in which the two of you combine black and white volcanic sand collected from Santorini beaches.
journey.reaction: A local touch, mentioned once and not overdone. Nice, but it is a detail for a ceremony of thirty people.

journey.quote: Katikies Hotels list micro weddings in Santorini as a package idea, describing small ceremonies with Aegean views, planned and managed by its events and concierge team.
journey.reaction: Micro weddings and package ideas. Early on, the page is already telling me who it is really for, and it is not us.

journey.quote: The figures below are for Naxos, the nearest official station, so read them as a guide to the neighbourhood rather than a forecast for the caldera.
journey.reaction: Careful and precise. My assistant took 'May or September, ceremony late in the day' from the whole section, which is all I needed.

journey.quote: Plan water, light fabrics, shade and air-conditioned rest for guests, and set a summer ceremony later in the day.
journey.reaction: Practical and right for elderly relatives in heat. This is the kind of thinking I want on the ground.

journey.quote: A flat venue fee includes exclusive use of the chosen event spaces, furniture, set-up, breakdown and staffing.
journey.reaction: Exclusive use of a space, not the property. Strangers would still be on the next terrace. For us that is the first thing that rules a venue out.

journey.quote: A private villa gives you one address for the wedding party and a ceremony no one else walks through.
journey.reaction: This line understands privacy. The wedding party in one villa, nobody walking through. I would use this for the family the night before.

journey.quote: If Santorini's caldera terraces feel too small for your numbers, compare [Mykonos wedding venues](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues) and [Paros wedding venues](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/paros-wedding-venues) before you decide.
journey.reaction: Honest, and I respect that it doesn't pretend. But it sends me off to another island instead of telling me how a large wedding could still work here.

journey.quote: On the caldera, space is scarce.
journey.reaction: Four words and it tells me the truth. Understated, and I trust it more for it.

journey.quote: Above that, you are choosing between a standing reception, splitting the events across more than one space, or a larger terrace such as the one at Venetsanos.
journey.reaction: A standing reception for my grandmother is not an option. Splitting the family across spaces is not either. About 100 seated is still a third of our list. The answer for us seems to be the takeover and buyout lines below, but the page never puts them forward as the route for a large wedding.

journey.quote: Katikies lists a hotel takeover among its event types, and the Canaves Collection lists exclusives and buyouts among its events and weddings options.
journey.reaction: Now we are talking. Takeover and buyout are the words I was looking for. My assistant marked Katikies and Canaves to ask about.

journey.quote: From the airport, guests can travel on by public bus or taxi.
journey.reaction: Public bus. For our guests. It is accurate, but it pitches the reader as an ordinary traveller.

journey.quote: In most cases you carry your own luggage up and down stairs on ferries.
journey.reaction: Our guests will not be on a ferry carrying luggage. This is advice for a different wedding.

journey.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness.
journey.reaction: My assistant or the family office handles this. I skipped the section; it is long for me, but fine for whoever does the paperwork.

journey.quote: **Exclusive use.** Will the space, the venue or the whole property be closed to other guests, and what does exclusive use cover?
journey.reaction: The right question, finally framed at property level. I would add 'and for how many days', because we would want it for the whole weekend, not just the evening.

journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: Correct and discreet. Nothing important about our family should sit in a chat thread.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person is right. 'Quotes in AUD' tells me again this is written for an Australian couple with a set budget, not for a family in Dubai, Sydney and London.

journey.quote: **Venue fee versus package.** Some venues charge a flat venue fee covering spaces, furniture, set-up, breakdown and staffing, while others work from wedding packages set out in a brochure.
journey.reaction: No prices, no 'value', which I like. But 'compare inclusions line by line' and brochures is how a package client shops. We would take the property and build from there.

journey.quote: Very.
journey.reaction: The one confident answer in the FAQ is about small weddings. That says it all about where Santorini fits.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: Quiet close, no pressure, which I prefer. 'For Australian couples' narrows it again; my family is partly in Sydney, but most of our guests are not.

unanswered_questions: Can Katikies or Canaves be taken over in full for three days, and could a takeover seat 200 to 400 across its spaces?
Is there any property on Santorini that can seat 300 for dinner in one place?
Can Grace Hotel's full buyout be combined with a dinner elsewhere for the larger guest list?
Can our own caterer or chefs come into a hotel or winery for family dietary and cultural requirements?
Would a planner recommend Santorini for our numbers at all, or move us to Mykonos?

turn_offs_found.quote: Katikies Hotels list micro weddings in Santorini as a package idea, describing small ceremonies with Aegean views, planned and managed by its events and concierge team.
turn_offs_found.why: Packages and micro weddings early in the guide frame the reader as someone choosing from a hotel's menu. There is no discount talk, but it positions me as a standard package client.

turn_offs_found.quote: Some venues charge a flat venue fee covering spaces, furniture, set-up, breakdown and staffing, while others work from wedding packages set out in a brochure.
turn_offs_found.why: The cost section is built around comparing brochures and inclusions. For a family taking a whole property, packages are not how decisions are made, so the section reads as aimed at someone else.

turn_offs_found.quote: In most cases you carry your own luggage up and down stairs on ferries.
turn_offs_found.why: Ferry luggage and public buses are housekeeping for self-managed guests. It adds length without anything my family would act on, and it lowers the sense that this is a premium service.

would_share_with: My assistant, to ask Katikies and Canaves about a full takeover and how many they could seat across it
My mother, for the private villa line and the late-day ceremony advice for older guests

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [plan your Santorini wedding with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet, no 'from' price, no pressure, and one person start to finish is right. But the page tells me Santorini is built for 15 to 60 guests and keeps saying AUD and Australian couples. I would not fill in a web form myself; my assistant might, through a referral.

top_3_changes: In Step 4, after the line on standing receptions and split events, give the takeover and buyout route its own sentence as the path for larger guest lists, drawing together what the draft already says about Grace Hotel's full buyout, the Katikies hotel takeover and the Canaves exclusives and buyouts, so a reader planning for well over 100 sees a way forward on Santorini before being sent to Mykonos or Paros.
Add 'and for how many days' to the Exclusive use question in Step 7 and the matching checklist line, so the question covers a whole wedding weekend rather than one evening.

Trim the self-managed traveller details in Step 5 (public bus, carrying luggage on ferries) or recast them as a guest-briefing note, and drop 'for Australian couples' from the closing advisor line so families travelling from elsewhere still feel addressed.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, cares about scale, closure and discretion)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; every turn-off has a why

Title, deferred business details (fees, commissions, private logistics, security, scale proof, on-the-ground team, call first) and absent prices not treated as must-fix; no request to explain sourcing or not-published items

assumptions: Layla is weighing Santorini for a 200 to 400 guest wedding; the persona card doesn't name a destination.
Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour.
